The Power Behind Your Faction

While characters act as individuals in the world, factions operate on a larger scale.

To organize expeditions, build infrastructure, and confront major threats, a faction must spend Operations Points, often shortened to OP.

Operations Points represent the collective capacity of your organization to act.

They reflect many different forms of power, including:

• manpower
• logistical support
• political influence
• economic resources
• coordination and planning

When your faction spends OP, it is mobilizing all of these forces to accomplish something significant.

What OP Is Used For

Operations Points fuel most major faction actions.

Your faction may spend OP to:

• develop hexes
• construct infrastructure
• conduct raids
• organize large expeditions
• support strategic activities

If characters represent the hands of the faction, OP represents its strength and momentum.

Earning Operations Points

Factions generate OP over time through the strength and stability of their territory.

Common sources of OP include:

• developed hexes
• functional infrastructure
• stable communities
• successful faction activities

As your territory grows and becomes more organized, your faction gains greater capacity to act.

Spending Operations Points

When your faction attempts something large or coordinated, it will usually require OP.

Some examples include:

• launching a raid against a powerful enemy
• restoring infrastructure in a damaged hex
• organizing large-scale travel or expeditions
• supporting major strategic activities

OP represents the effort and coordination required to make these actions possible.

Because OP is limited, factions must decide carefully where to invest their resources.

Managing OP

Operations Points are one of the most important resources your faction controls.

A faction with strong OP reserves can:

• respond quickly to threats
• expand into new territory
• support large operations

A faction with little OP must act cautiously and choose its priorities carefully.

Managing OP well is often the difference between steady progress and dangerous stagnation.

The Flow of OP

Over the course of a campaign, OP moves through a simple cycle.

Generate OP from Territory
        ↓
Plan Strategic Actions
        ↓
Spend OP to Act
        ↓
Resolve Outcomes
        ↓
Territory Changes
        ↓
Generate OP Again

Success often leads to stronger territory, which produces more OP and allows the faction to attempt even larger projects.

OP and Strategy

Because OP is limited, factions must constantly make strategic choices.

You may need to decide whether to:

• expand into new hexes
• strengthen existing territory
• confront dangerous enemies
• prepare for future threats

Every decision shapes the direction of your faction and the future of the world.

OP and the Great Work

Operations Points represent more than simple resources.

They reflect the collective will of people working together to repair reality.

When factions spend OP to stabilize hexes, build communities, or confront corruption, they are contributing directly to the Great Work.

Each action pushes the world closer to restoration.

What Players Should Remember

Three ideas define Operations Points.

1 — OP is faction energy

It represents the power your organization can bring to bear.

2 — OP enables big actions

Major faction activities usually require OP.

3 — OP requires careful management

How you spend OP shapes the future of the campaign.

In Simple Terms

Operations Points are the fuel that powers your faction.

They determine what your organization can accomplish and how quickly it can grow.

Used wisely, OP allows your faction to transform small successes into lasting change.
